question: Who has the administrative control over the Postal Department in India?
option1: Secretary of the Department of Posts
option3: Director General of Posts New Delhi
explanation: The Postal Department is under the administrative control of the Director General of Posts New Delhi who also functions as the Chairman of the Postal Board and Secretary of the Department of Posts.

question: What are the three classes of Post Offices described in the guide?
option1: Primary Offices Secondary Offices Tertiary Offices
option2: Head Post Offices Sub-Post Offices Branch Post Offices
option3: Central Offices Local Offices Auxiliary Offices
option4: Main Post Offices Regional Offices Delivery Offices
explanation: Post Offices are divided into three classes: Head Post Offices Sub-Post Offices and Branch Post Offices. Each class has specific roles and facilities particularly regarding the services offered to the public.

question: What is a Night Post Office authorized to do according to the guide?
option1: Function only for parcel dispatch without delivery services
option2: Operate only regular business hours with no special services
option3: Close fully on Sundays and National Holidays
option4: Extend working hours up to 8:30 PM book registered articles and sell stamps even on Sundays
explanation: Night Post Offices may have extended hours up to 8:30 PM work on Sundays with restricted services and handle registered articles and sales of stamps as authorized by the Director-General.

question: What is the minimum and maximum weight allowed for a letter sent by post?
option1: Maximum weight 5 kilograms minimum length 20 cm and 14 cm in other dimensions
option2: Maximum weight 2 kilograms minimum length 11 cm and 7 cm in other dimensions
option3: Maximum weight 10 kilograms minimum length 15 cm and 10 cm in other dimensions
option4: No limit on weight minimum size 5 cm by 5 cm
explanation: A letter should not weigh more than 2 kilograms and must conform to specific size limits including a minimum of 11 cm by 7 cm in other than roll form to be accepted for transmission.
